themes.title: AI capex supercycle hits records: memory, chips, debt
themes.summary: The AI buildout is now showing up in hard money: Samsung posted a record operating profit of about $80bn on high-bandwidth-memory demand, Broadcom is planning its next blockbuster AI-chip financing after the $60bn Anthropic deal, and China is racing to site data centres on cheap energy in Inner Mongolia. Risk is also being priced: SpaceX credit default swaps jumped on a reported $40bn Nvidia-chip purchase plan, and a Nvidia-backed data-centre IPO is struggling to close.
themes.angle: Supply side of AI is monetising; the open question is when demand-side ROI shows up.

themes.title: GCC bets on AI workforce and sovereign models
themes.summary: Abu Dhabi launched AiNative, training 23,000 government staff in AI by 2027 with OpenAI, Microsoft and MBZUAI, while a new UAE-built model, Falcon-Emirati, targets how Emiratis actually speak. Dubai's Crown Prince opened a Create AI Agents Championship for ideas serving global good, and Saudi AI-localisation startup Echelon raised a fresh round.
themes.angle: Gulf governments are buying AI capability at the workforce layer - the region's real moat play.

themes.title: Agentic AI starts attacking banks' deposit economics
themes.summary: An FT analysis argues that AI agents which shop for better savings rates could strip up to $500bn of cheap deposits out of banks, while The Information asks why the automation payoff is still invisible in the data. Same coin, two faces: the technology can now disintermediate core franchises before most enterprises have scaled real ROI.
themes.angle: "Where's the automation?" and "agents are eating deposits" are the same question from different chairs.

themes.title: Model releases hit the price-performance frontier
themes.summary: Anthropic shipped Claude Haiku 5.5, its fastest, cheapest small model for high-volume, cost-sensitive work, as GPT-6 rolls out globally in ChatGPT with an Intelligent UI. Mistral Large 4 now ranks alongside GPT-6 Luna and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and Google is broadening AI-content watermarking.
themes.angle: Inference economics keeps falling - enterprise buyers should re-benchmark contracts now.

themes.title: UAE-US AI diplomacy and Gulf AI economy widen
themes.summary: The UAE and US held talks to deepen AI, quantum and space cooperation, while ADIPEC 2026 gathers global tech CEOs as AI reshapes energy operations. IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva warned that AI-investment risk, debt above 100% of GDP and potentially $100 oil threaten global growth - a macro mix with direct Gulf exposure.
themes.angle: AI is now state-to-state economics in the Gulf, not just vendor strategy.

themes.title: AI capital rotates: funds, biology and world models
themes.summary: Capital placement is broadening beyond datacentres: ex-White House AI adviser Sriram Krishnan is raising a $500m fund, Google DeepMind, Meta and Isomorphic are investing $300m in Biohub's $1.8bn AI-biology effort, and a former ByteDance intern's $200m stealth lab is taking on world-model pioneers.
themes.angle: Next-phase AI bets are rotating to world models and biology, not just infrastructure.

themes.title: Consumer AI: PCs, games, hotels and teen safety
themes.summary: Microsoft unveiled Nvidia-powered Windows laptops aimed at on-device AI after Apple's breakout hit, Google launched a text-to-video-game platform with Unity, and Radisson brought hotel discovery into ChatGPT via an Accenture-built plugin. Common Sense Media is urging OpenAI to keep teens off ChatGPT over safeguard concerns, and a Reuters/Ipsos poll found most US voters think leaders are not taking AI risks seriously enough.
themes.angle: The AI PC and app-layer distribution wars are now fully commercial.
